newsitem.title: USA: Exxon reports record quarterly profits.
newsitem.headline: Exxon reports record quarterly profits.

text.p: Exxon Corp said Monday it had record quarterly earnings of $2.49 billion in 1996's final quarter, adding this was up 49 percent from a year earlier.
Annual profits were up 16 percent to $7.51 billion, reaching a record for the second consecutive year, it said.

The company also said 1996 full year capital and exploration spending was $9.25 billion -- including $2.63 billion in the fourth quarter -- up from $8.97 billion in 1995. "Expenditures in 1997 should be at similar levels, as attractive investment opportunities continue to be developed in each of the major business segments," Exxon said.
The company said about half the gain in fourth quarter profits from last year's $1.68 billion came on tax related gains of $410 million. There were $90 million of credits a year earlier.

Relative to 1995's final quarter, exploration and production earnings in the latest quarter rose on the strength of increased natural gas sales in Europe, lower production expenses, and higher crude oil and natural gas prices.
Exxon said downstream earnings declined despite higher sales worldwide as industry margins were generally weaker than in the fourth quarter of 1995.

The chemicals business achieved record fourth quarter sales, the company said. While commodity chemical prices were stronger than in 1995, margins were squeezed as a result of increased feedstock costs.
Exxon said earnings from other operations decreased relative to the 1995's final quarter due to significantly lower copper prices.
During the fourth quarter, the company said, it purchased 2.8 million of its common shares at a cost of $266 million.
During all of 1996, 9.2 million shares were purchased for the company's treasury at a cost of $801 million.
